title: Slip failure response
description: The failure shape a client MUST be able to read. `code` is constrained to the shape of a code rather than to the version 1 list, because a client that can only parse codes it already knows would discard the publisher's message over a value it could have rendered, and would report a defined condition as an unreadable response. What an endpoint may send is narrowed by slip-error-response-endpoint.schema.json.

type.description: Discriminates a failure from the shapes GET and POST return on success.

version.description: Major version of the Slip protocol this endpoint speaks. Present here so a response a client cannot read still says what it was.

message.description: Plain text for the person. No markup, no stack traces, no internal identifiers.

field.description: The name of the parameter at fault, so a client can attach the message to the field that caused it.

code.description: The shape of a code. Matches the pattern reason.code uses in discovery, so one rule covers both.

fieldNamesTheRejectedParameter.description: field explains which submitted value was rejected, so it is meaningless unless a submitted value was.
